findings.problem: load_sensors fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), logging (println!), parsing, and domain construction into a single function
findings.failure_mode: pure logic cannot be tested without real filesystem access; logging leaks into calculations; the shell boundary is violated making the function untestable and non-reusable
findings.fix: split into a pure parse_sensors(&[String]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, SensorError> and a shell load_sensors(path: &str) that handles I/O, logging, and error mapping

findings.problem: No error types exist; all failures (file not found, parse error, index out of bounds, allocation) collapse into panics via unwrap
findings.failure_mode: caller cannot distinguish between missing file, malformed CSV, missing fields, or invalid values; no recovery or retry semantics possible
findings.fix: define enum SensorError { Io(io::Error), InvalidLine(usize), Parse(usize), Overflow(usize) } and return Result<Vec<Record>, SensorError>

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on missing file or permission error
findings.failure_mode: process aborts with panic instead of returning a typed I/O error; downstream callers have no chance to recover
findings.fix: return Result from load_sensors and use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(SensorError::Io)?

findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV data causes panic instead of returning a typed Parse error for that line
findings.fix: use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| SensorError::Parse(idx))? with the line index

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses index without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: empty or single-field CSV lines cause panic via index out of bounds
findings.fix: use parts.get(0).ok_or(SensorError::InvalidLine(idx))? or pattern match on split_once

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses index without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: lines with only one CSV field cause panic via index out of bounds

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 is a lossy conversion that silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: sensor value 70000 becomes 4464 without any error or warning; data integrity is silently corrupted
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed).map_err(|_| SensorError::Overflow(idx))? to reject out-of-range values

findings.problem: raw string primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors; callers can construct invalid Record directly and split(',') without validation lets any malformed data reach domain logic
findings.failure_mode: no type-level guarantee that Record::name is non-empty or Record::value fits u16; the parse boundary is leaky so invalid domain states are representable
findings.fix: define a private Record { name: DomainName, value: DomainValue } with smart constructor Record::from_csv_line(line: &str) -> Result<Record, SensorError> that validates invariants

findings.problem: No domain cap on number of records, no try_reserve, no file size limit, and Vec<String> is materialized from every line without reuse
findings.failure_mode: malicious or large CSV files cause unbounded memory allocation; no defense against resource exhaustion; every line allocates a new Vec<String> and multiple String copies
findings.fix: accept a max_records cap; use Vec::new() with values.try_reserve(max_records).map_err(|_| SensorError::Allocation)?; reuse a String buffer across iterations; use split_once instead of split+collect

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds stdout I/O in the mapping closure that transforms CSV data
findings.failure_mode: parsing logic has a side effect on stdout; breaks functional purity; pollutes output when called from non-CLI contexts; makes unit tests brittle
findings.fix: remove println! entirely from pure logic; if logging is needed, pass a tracing::info! call through a logger abstraction in the shell layer only

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a Vec for every line; split_once is mandatory for one-separator grammars per functional-core-performance reference
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary allocation per line plus unbounded split on lines with extra commas silently drops data instead of erroring
findings.fix: use let (_name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(SensorError::InvalidLine(idx))?; then parse value_str

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for load_sensors
findings.failure_mode: cannot verify performance characteristics, allocation budget, or hot-path behavior; no baseline to measure against
findings.fix: add benches/sensor_load.rs with criterion or similar, measuring iterations/sec, bytes/sec, and allocations per iteration

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sensors performance characteristics
no profiler data showing allocation hotspots in the parsing path
no allocation evidence proving bounded memory usage under large or hostile input
no second-ring evidence for any zero-cost or bounds-check removal claims
no command-truth evidence (cargo fmt, clippy, test) was run or reported
residual_risk: Static review identified 10 BLOCKER violations across all Holzman absolute laws: hidden I/O in pure logic, no typed error taxonomy, two unwrap panic surfaces, two unchecked index accesses, one lossy cast, leaky parse boundary, unbounded allocation without try_reserve, and split instead of split_once. No commands were run. Full delivery requires repairing all BLOCKER findings, adding typed errors, splitting shell from core, removing all unwrap/panic/println, using checked conversions, enforcing domain caps with try_reserve, and establishing benchmark evidence. Without repair, the code cannot satisfy panic freedom, bounded resources, or functional core architecture.
